Nora: Heads-up: shadow bringup of new reranker-v4 (float16) shows MRR stable but NDCG@5 dips ~1.8% on cross-domain set (docs from help + KB). Quick summary below.
Luis: Which cross-domain split? Is this the help-to-kb mix we use in stagebench?
Nora: Yes stagebench-mix v3, split ratio 60/40 help/kb. Baseline (v3-fp32)=0.701, reranker-v4-fp16=0.688 at ndcg@5. mrr@10 0.592 -> 0.590.
Tanya: Could be short answers in help docs losing precision in fp16 causing top1 swaps. Do we have per-slice top1 frequency?
perf-bot: report: top1_freq_help=0.412 baseline / 0.395 v4, top1_freq_kb=0.328 / 0.326
Nora: That suggests help docs impacted more. Error bars? reruns show similar.
Luis: Any changes in tokenization/repipelines?
Nora: No. Model conversion: float32->float16 with fp16-quant wrapper but we also applied fused attention kernel which changes numerical ordering slightly.
Tanya: Let's run targeted ablation: float16 without fused kernel, and fused kernel with float32 emulation to isolate.
Nora: Running: 1) v4 fp16 no-fuse -> ndcg@5 0.697 (better) 2) v4 fp16 + fuse-emulate-fp32 -> 0.694. So fuse kernel numerics look like main culprit.
Luis: Makes sense. Fused kernels reorder reductions; ranking depends on tiny score deltas. For production we can: a) keep fused kernel for latency but add a deterministic rank-stable path for top-k re-ranking b) adjust thresholding in reranker to reduce numeric sensitivity.
Tanya: Also add a CI check: when introducing kernel changes, run a quick shadow on stagebench and ensure ndcg variation <1%.
Nora: I'll open PRs: (Nora) add kernel-stability quickcheck in bench; (Luis) prototype top-k secondary re-score fallback; (Tanya) update CI gate with post-kernel sanity.
perf-bot: "note: fused-attn rollouts should include ndcg_unit_test; patch queued"
Nora: Thanks team. We'll keep observing during canary.
